codefuseRole: external comparison target only; never used as a fixture-design oracle in this audit

discovery: git ls-files filtered by arm64|aarch64 (576 tracked paths)
per-directory arm64/aarch64 content grep over tests/**
direct reading of each evidence class to determine WHAT is asserted, not only where the file lives

assertionClassVocabulary.unit-decoder-encoding: asserts decoder/encoder bit-field domains, operand shapes, mnemonic ownership on synthetic or enumerated words
assertionClassVocabulary.unit-effect-classification: asserts machine-effect registry families (flags/memory/control/...) for an instruction form
assertionClassVocabulary.unit-abi-classification: asserts ABI argument/return classification and register/stack allocation without executing a program
assertionClassVocabulary.synthetic-loader-parse: asserts ELF/Mach-O/PE parser invariants on hand-built byte fixtures emitted inside the test
assertionClassVocabulary.owned-binary-end-to-end: asserts product behaviour over an owned source -> toolchain -> binary artifact whose sha256 is pinned
assertionClassVocabulary.compiler-truth-semantic: asserts decompiled semantics against an independently evaluated source-level expected expression for real compiler output
assertionClassVocabulary.frozen-corpus-semantic: asserts semantic-path/provenance/hard-zero counters over a frozen multi-architecture corpus
assertionClassVocabulary.presentation-only: asserts rendered text/labels/UI formatting, not semantics
assertionClassVocabulary.provenance-identity-contract: asserts identity/schema/fail-closed contracts that are architecture-independent or lightly ARM64-typed

gateVocabulary.check: reachable from `npm run check` (the repository gate)
gateVocabulary.test: reachable from `npm test` which is itself called by check
gateVocabulary.workflow-only: executed by a GitHub workflow, not by the local canonical gate
gateVocabulary.manual: requires an explicit operator command or an external artifact

evidence.whatIsAsserted: A frozen candidate word corpus (376,186 candidate words / 375,875 unique, candidateSha256 bound in the locked inventory) is re-decoded through the deployed Capstone ARM64 session; every valid in-profile encoding must be owned by exactly one canonical effect family, and the fallback/unmatched-family path must be proven unreachable by a negative proof. Scope-shrink and corpus-shrink guards reject a smaller corpus.
evidence.generalizationValue: high for decode coverage; it proves nothing about decompiler end-to-end recovery

evidence.whatIsAsserted: Finite enumerated encoding families per family. Example: the integer denominator asserts encodingFamilyCount=39, encodingCaseCount=68,901, mnemonicCount=83, and equality between the mnemonic denominator and the shipped ARM64_INTEGER_EFFECT_MNEMONICS registry, decoded one batch at a time through Capstone and classified by the production lifter.
evidence.generalizationValue: high for instruction semantics ownership; synthetic encoding enumeration, not compiled-source behaviour

evidence.whatIsAsserted: PAuth/authenticated-load/eretaa-eretab effects, BTI landing-pad policy, implicit-x30 modifiers, strict register identity, and architecture/ABI pairing fail-closed for arm64e.
evidence.generalizationValue: medium; arm64e is retained as a supplementary lane in most corpora

paths: tests/machine-effects/arm64-*.test.mjs (119 arm64-named files, excluding the denominators above)
evidence.whatIsAsserted: Per-mnemonic-family operand and modifier domains: addsub immediate, MOV/MOVZ/MOVN aliases, ADRP/ADR operand shape, bitfield, logical structured encoding, multiply/divide, scalar immediate modifiers, width/shift validation, SIMD lane and modifier encodings, prefetch/PRFM register offsets, system/barrier selectors, trap imm16, TBZ bit domains, btype rename state.
evidence.generalizationValue: high breadth, low end-to-end depth

evidence.area: ARM64 issue-specific regression tests in machine-effects
evidence.whatIsAsserted: Each file pins one externally reported ARM64 defect (fault modelling, NZCV absence, exclusive/acquire forms, PAC state) at the effect-registry boundary.
evidence.generalizationValue: high for the specific defect class; these are exact executable regressions, not generalizations

evidence.whatIsAsserted: Claim-local permitted/forbidden outcome sets for a declared litmus universe; explicitly not absolute ISA truth.
evidence.generalizationValue: medium; bounded to declared litmus programs

evidence.whatIsAsserted: 135 cases = 3 architectures x 15 source functions x {O0,O1,O2}. For the 45 ARM64 cases the decompiler must take the shared semantic path, emit AST + source map, carry complete expression-history/phase8-projection/render provenance, and must not regress the frozen pre-Phase-8 baseline. 10 named ARM64 cases are expanded into a representative end-to-end denominator.
evidence.arm64Role: the primary decompiler end-to-end corpus for ARM64
evidence.generalizationValue: high but structurally limited: the ARM64 lane representation is `assembly` text, parsed by tests/tools with js/arm64.js parseOperands before entering the public decompile() facade, whereas the x86_64 and riscv64 lanes freeze `machine-bytes` from a final ELF link and are decoded by the shipped Capstone artifact. No ARM64 lane exercises loader -> capstone -> decoded-instruction -> semantic pipeline.

evidence.area: Phase 8 frozen hard-zero counters and verifier
evidence.gate: check for the metric/verifier contract tests; verify.mjs is a separate exact-SHA command
evidence.whatIsAsserted: Hard-zero counters compared against a frozen pre-Phase-8 baseline: semanticMismatchCount, provenanceLossCount, unknownSafetyRegressionCount, renderProvenanceLossCount, renderProvenanceUnboundCount. Determinism is proved by two independent in-process corpus runs sharing one time budget (MEASUREMENT_TIME_BUDGET_MS = 20000).
evidence.generalizationValue: high; this is the strongest existing hard-zero-counter pattern in the repository and is reusable for a new suite

evidence.area: compiler-truth: real multi-language, multi-optimization ARM64 semantic truth
evidence.gate: manual / workflow-only (referenced only by .github/workflows/ghidra-differential.yml; not in npm test nor npm run check)
evidence.whatIsAsserted: Real clang/clang++/swiftc output for targets aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu and arm64-apple-ios13.0 across -O0..-Oz. The suite parses compiler assembly into a model, runs the product decompiler through a guarded deterministic boundary, then evaluates the recovered return expression over a boundary value set ([0,1,-1,2,-2,0x7fffffff,0x80000000,0xffffffff,0x12345678]) and compares against an independently computed expected value.
evidence.arm64Role: the only existing real-compiler ARM64 semantic oracle with language and optimization matrix coverage
evidence.generalizationValue: very high in design; currently outside the canonical gate and still assembly-text based rather than linked-binary based

evidence.area: SCPA owned ARM64 assembled-ELF end-to-end fixtures
evidence.whatIsAsserted: Owned AArch64 assembly source is assembled and linked into a real ELF with a pinned sha256 for both source and binary plus a recorded rebuild command. The test then runs the actual ELF parser, the deployed Capstone WASM decoder, an actual worker thread, the opt-in scoped ARM64 producer, and the public QueryAPI; it asserts function extents, demand-query publication, integer-fragment/range-proof nodes, replay integrity and byte binding, and invalidation on symbol revision or binary epoch change.
evidence.arm64Role: the only loader+decoder+analysis end-to-end ARM64 path exercised today
evidence.generalizationValue: high structural value (real binary, pinned provenance, explicit non-claims) but it is hand-written assembly, 3 fixtures, and it does not assert decompiler source semantics

evidence.area: Phase 4 binary loader tests touching ARM64
evidence.whatIsAsserted: ELF64 / Mach-O (incl. arm64_32, fat, chained fixups, unwind xdata) / PE32+ ARM64 container invariants: pointer widths, indirect symbol pointer sizes, load-command ranges, page alignment, section virtual layout, relocation whitelists, function-start discovery. Fixtures are almost entirely constructed in-test with DataView byte writers; exactly 1 of the 197 phase4/binary files reads a checked-in binary fixture.
evidence.generalizationValue: high breadth at the parser boundary; no real-vendor ARM64 binary is parsed by this suite

evidence.area: Public CodeFuse ARM64 benchmark (external comparison target)
evidence.gate: manual (npm run benchmark:public) and pr-fast-gate; tests/public-benchmark tests run in npm test
evidence.whatIsAsserted: 160 frozen ARM64 cases = 8 programs x {clang,gcc} x {O0,O1,O2,O3,Os} x {debug,no-debug}; the published reference is an IDA Pro artifact, so the suite is a similarity/normalization comparison, not an independent semantic oracle.
evidence.generalizationValue: must NOT be used as a fixture-design oracle: its reference outputs and exact case set are the overfitting target this audit exists to prevent

evidence.whatIsAsserted: 12 named cases across 6 language recipes (C/C++/ObjC/Swift/Rust/Go) with source sha256 pinning, closed 6-language/12-case set, 28 metrics, 2 toolchain slots. The runner is an offline source-and-denominator gate: it re-verifies source hashes, checks a wrong-oracle sentinel is rejected, and reports every cell UNMEASURED with victoryEstablished=false, binaryTwinsVerified=false, nativeCompetitorsRun=false.
evidence.arm64Role: the existing language-recipe foundation that a new suite must reuse rather than duplicate
evidence.generalizationValue: high for provenance discipline and language breadth; zero executed measurement today

evidence.whatIsAsserted: Argument/return classification and placement: wide integral register pairs, stack natural alignment, return width authority, v8-v15 clobber, HFA/HVA handling, Darwin compact stack slots, long double, variadic word slots, ILP32/arm64_32 pointer widths, indirect (sret) returns, entry-bank prototypes, required profile matrix.
evidence.generalizationValue: high coverage of the classification rules; the classification is asserted as a unit, almost never against a real compiled call site

evidence.area: Phase 7 alias/memory corpus and discovery lanes
evidence.whatIsAsserted: 19 named alias/memory fixtures declared across mandatory lanes arm64/riscv64/x86_64 with format lanes elf/macho/pe, with explicit truth values per pointer-pair query (no / may-or-weaker / must) and an expectStrong flag separating strong answers from soundness.
evidence.generalizationValue: high for the alias dimension; the arm64 lane shares the frozen fixture shape with the other architectures

evidence.area: Phase 4/10/12 ARM64 semantic and runtime regressions
evidence.whatIsAsserted: ARM64 structure lane access sizes, atomic RMW semantic blocks, pointer masks, arm64_32 pointer widths, vtable pointer width, PC wrap on branch targets.
evidence.generalizationValue: high for the specific invariants; these are exact regressions, not holdouts

evidence.whatIsAsserted: Mixed: operand/encoding domains (ADR/ADRP, direct branch target alignment), LDTR/STTR family, SP/FP aliasing, MTE tag instructions, address wraparound, negative hex display presentation, and legacy ARM64 proof surfaces.
evidence.generalizationValue: medium; unit-level with no corpus

evidence.whatIsAsserted: Semantic IR lowering of ARM64 machine effects, NZCV/ADC/SBC flag preservation, FMOV bit patterns, control-target cardinality, and architecture neutrality of the shared IR.
evidence.generalizationValue: medium; architecture-neutral by design, so it deliberately does not add ARM64-specific generalization

evidence.gate: manual (npm run fixtures:large / npm run accuracy)
evidence.whatIsAsserted: Three sha256-pinned multi-megabyte binaries (28/46/63 MB, iOS game images) are parsed, audited, benchmarked and scored by the accuracy harness with a python oracle. The artifacts are absent from the repository (each path holds a 62-69 byte placeholder), so none of this runs in the canonical gate.
evidence.arm64Role: the only large real-world ARM64 Mach-O corpus
evidence.generalizationValue: very high in principle; unexecuted in every normal gate and therefore not a regression

evidence.area: Language/format metadata suites with ARM64 fixtures
evidence.whatIsAsserted: ObjC class/metaclass/protocol metadata, Swift vtable/witness-table/generic metadata, Rust v0 symbol mangling, Go rtype/pclntab/ABI metadata, with ARM64 pointer-width variants.
evidence.generalizationValue: high per-language; metadata presence is asserted, not decompiled source semantics

evidence.whatIsAsserted: A locked inventory over 4 profiles (arm64:a64, arm64e:a64+pac, x86_64:long-64, riscv64:rv64imc) with fullIsaCoverageIncluded=false, explicitDecoderGapCount=0 and blockingGapCount=0 as terminality conditions. It explicitly rejects any claim of full-ISA coverage.
evidence.arm64Role: the terminality contract for ARM64 effect coverage
evidence.generalizationValue: high as a false-green guard: it forbids equating registry ownership with full ISA or with product semantics

dimensionMap.note: Instruction-family ownership is exhaustively enumerated (376k candidate words; 68,901 integer encoding cases) but entirely at the decoder/effect-registry boundary.

constraintsObserved: No production code and no existing test file was modified by this audit.
CodeFuse reference outputs, binary hashes, case names, function names and addresses were read only to size the external target; none were copied into any proposed fixture shape in this stage.
